canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Identifying Null and Full Angles
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/867b3664e93f42c55a2f97dc28bf66794484e226981632c85f725926cec77def.png)

What type of angle is $\angle RST,$ shown in the figure above?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the vertex of $\angle RST$ is point $S,$ not point $T.$ So $\angle RST$ is *not* a straight angle.

As a result, the two rays $\overset{\longrightarrow}{SR}$ and $\overset{\longrightarrow}{ST}$ of our angle coincide. So, we can think of $\angle RST$ as:

- A *null* angle, assuming it doesn't turn at all.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/a8916a724d4463bf2047c919b73770160d3124838b61af0dcdc2b9e04322381a.png)

- A *full* angle, assuming it makes one full turn.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/9cd768b4361e95a18ffa52d6315fb5ea6cd0cf6784bc4c9e12b1bae1f6566755.png)

So, the answer is "Null" or "Full."

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Some angles have special names.

- A **right angle** has a measure of $90^\circ.$ It corresponds to one-quarter of a full turn.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/155a1d6d2abd868b05674dec47ef4b20a5147d30cd328a5ba53d00dea271d65c.png)

- A **straight angle**, which is just a straight line, has a measure of $180^\circ.$ It corresponds to one-half of a full turn.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/2423950f80de8354aee74c4f1daa6e42cf376caa0365307c76ebc7e09f96c8cf.png)

- A **null angle** has a measure of $0^\circ.$ You can imagine "closing" the angle until the two sides of the angle overlap. In this case, we don't have any turn, so its measure is zero!

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/f86b7c1b7ba758fb6b07b6aeabd03395d29103b45e4cd220444b675f70a6e630.png)

- A **full angle** has a measure of $360^\circ.$ You can imagine "opening" the angle until one of the sides goes all the way around. So, this is the angle between a ray and itself after it has made one full turn.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131901/assets/cbc9e288f4d3905357539a221954328ef0ac799531fab62f034364d32a7c0f29.png)

On a diagram, null and full angles can look the same, so it is up to us what we choose to call it.
